title: Prone positioning in ARDS
one_line_summary: Prone positioning reduces **mortality** in mechanically ventilated severe ARDS when applied early for >= 16 hours daily, while awake prone positioning reduces intubation in non-intubated COVID-19 hypoxemic failure when maintained >= 8-10 hours daily.
key_pearls: Early and prolonged prone positioning (**>= 16 hours/day**) **significantly** reduces **28-day** and **90-day mortality** in mechanically ventilated patients with moderate-to-severe ARDS (**PaO2/FiO2 < 150 mmHg**, **PEEP >= 5 cmH2O**, **FiO2 >= 0.60**).

In non-intubated patients with COVID-19 acute hypoxemic respiratory failure on high-flow nasal cannula (**HFNC**), awake prone positioning reduces intubation rates, provided treatment adherence reaches **> 8-10 hours/day**.

Prone positioning improves gas exchange by enhancing *ventilation-perfusion matching*, relieving dorsal alveolar compression, and reducing regional lung stress and strain to prevent *ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI)*.
Standard protocolized stopping criteria require a sustained **PaO2/FiO2 >= 150 mmHg** with **PEEP <= 10 cmH2O** and **FiO2 <= 0.60** assessed **4 hours** after resupination to the supine position.

Unstable spinal fracture is the single widely accepted **absolute** contraindication to prone positioning; conditions like severe obesity or recent abdominal surgery are relative and manageable by experienced teams.

Pressure ulceration is the most common dose-dependent adverse event, whereas severe complications like accidental extubation or line dislodgement are rare when maneuvers are executed by **3-5 trained staff**.
population: Adult intubated and non-intubated patients with acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) or acute hypoxemic respiratory failure

sections.heading: Introduction and Historical Context
sections.content:
- Prone positioning (**PP**) was first described in **1976** as a rescue strategy for refractory hypoxemia in mechanically ventilated ARDS patients.
- Initial randomized controlled trials (**2001-2009**) failed to demonstrate **survival** benefits due to short session durations (**7-8 hours/day**), high tidal volume settings (**8-10 mL/kg**), and non-standardized mechanical ventilation.
- Individual patient data meta-analysis of early trials confirmed a **survival** benefit isolated to patients with severe hypoxemia (**PaO2/FiO2 < 100 mmHg**).
- The landmark **PROSEVA** trial (**2013**) demonstrated that early (**< 36 hours** post-intubation) and prolonged (**>= 16 hours/day**) PP combined with low tidal volume ventilation (**6 mL/kg PBW**) **significantly** reduced **28-day mortality** (**16.0%** vs **32.8%**, *p < 0.001*) and **90-day mortality** (**23.6%** vs **41.0%**, *p < 0.001*).
- The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the clinical adaptation of awake prone positioning (**APP**) for non-intubated hypoxemic patients.
section_pearls: Prone positioning shifted from a late rescue maneuver to an early primary lung-protective therapy following the PROSEVA trial.
Early trials failed to show benefit primarily due to insufficient proning duration (< 10 hours/day) and unprotective tidal volumes.

sections.heading: Pathophysiologic Mechanisms
sections.content:
- **Gas Exchange**: PP redistributes gravitational forces and relieves heart and mediastinal weight on dorsal lung regions, promoting dorsal alveolar recruitment and optimizing *ventilation-perfusion matching*.
- **Lung Protection**: Decreases ventral alveolar over-distension and homogenizes regional stress and strain, mitigating *ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI)* and *patient self-inflicted lung injury (P-SILI)*.
- **Hemodynamics**: Reduces right ventricular afterload and increases cardiac venous return, elevating cardiac output in preload-dependent patients.
- **Spontaneous Mechanics in APP**: Non-intubated patients show homogeneous ventilation distribution without marked dorsal redistribution; combining APP with **HFNC** improves ventilation-perfusion matching, whereas combining APP with **CPAP** or **NIV** yields minimal additional aeration gains due to baseline positive pressure recruitment.
section_pearls: Gas exchange improvements stem from gravity redistribution and cardiac decompression off dorsal alveoli.
Prone positioning unloads the right ventricle by reducing pulmonary vascular resistance and RV afterload.

sections.heading: Clinical Evidence in Intubated and Non-Intubated ARDS
sections.content:
- **Intubated Severe ARDS**: High-quality RCT evidence supports early prolonged PP (**>= 16 hours/day**) to improve **survival** in patients with **PaO2/FiO2 < 150 mmHg** and **PEEP >= 5 cmH2O**.
- **Veno-Venous ECMO**: RCTs (such as **PRONECMO**) demonstrate variable outcomes; successful weaning rates were **equivalent** (**44%** at **60 days**), though sub-analyses suggest greater benefit in non-COVID-19 ARDS etiologies.
- **Awake Prone Positioning (APP)**: A multinational meta-trial of **1,121** COVID-19 patients on **HFNC** showed that APP reduced intubation or death (**33%** vs **44%**).
- **Dose-Response Effect**: Clinical benefits in non-intubated patients are strictly dependent on daily duration, requiring prolonged sessions exceeding **8-10 hours/day** to reduce intubation and **mortality**.
section_pearls: Clinical success of awake prone positioning depends directly on achieving a daily threshold of > 8-10 hours/day.
Meta-trials confirm awake proning reduces intubation rates in COVID-19 patients on HFNC.

sections.heading: Guideline Recommendations and Implementation
sections.content:
- **Patient Selection**: **ESICM** (**2023**) and **ATS** (**2024**) strongly recommend PP in intubated ARDS patients with **PaO2/FiO2 < 150 mmHg** and **PEEP >= 5 cmH2O** after ventilation optimization.
- **Timing and Initiation**: PP should be initiated early after intubation following a brief stabilization period under lung-protective ventilation (**6 mL/kg PBW**).
- **Session Duration**: Sessions must be maintained for at least **16 consecutive hours/day**.
- **Discontinuation Criteria**: PP is stopped when **PaO2/FiO2 >= 150 mmHg** with **PEEP <= 10 cmH2O** and **FiO2 <= 0.60** is maintained for at least **4 hours** post-resupination in the supine position.
- **Neuromuscular Blockade**: **ESICM** strongly recommends against routine continuous infusion of *neuromuscular blocking agents (NMBAs)*, whereas **ATS** offers a conditional recommendation for their short-term adjunctive use.
section_pearls: Initiate proning early (< 36 hours) in patients with PaO2/FiO2 < 150 mmHg despite optimal PEEP.
Assess stopping criteria in the supine position 4 hours after resupination, not during active proning.

sections.heading: Adverse Events, Workload, and Safety Profile
sections.content:
- **Complications**: Pressure injuries are the most frequent dose-dependent side effect; facial edema, transient hypotension, device dislodgement, and upper limb peripheral nerve injuries occur less commonly.
- **Contraindications**: Unstable spinal fractures are the only **absolute** contraindication; relative contraindications (obesity, recent abdominal surgery, chest drains) do not preclude proning by experienced teams.
- **Operational Resource Needs**: Turning intubated patients requires **3-5 trained staff members** per maneuver; APP requires dedicated nursing coaching and adherence monitoring using tools like the **ROX index** (**SpO2/FiO2/respiratory rate**).
section_pearls: Unstable spinal trauma is the only absolute contraindication to prone positioning.
Manual turning requires 3-5 trained personnel to prevent tube and line dislodgement.

sections.heading: Future Directions and Ongoing Research
sections.content:
- **Non-COVID-19 AHRF**: Trials such as **PRONELIFE** (**n = 650**) and **NCT06966310** (**n = 1,078**) are evaluating whether APP reduces intubation in non-COVID-19 hypoxemic failure and pneumonia.
- **Mild-to-Moderate ARDS**: The **PROMILD** trial is evaluating whether early PP improves ventilator-free days in mild-to-moderate intubated ARDS.
- **Ultra-Prolonged Sessions**: Meta-analyses of prolonged sessions (**> 16 hours**, up to **24-120 hours**) show no **significant** reduction in **90-day mortality** compared to standard **16-hour** protocols.
section_pearls: Ongoing trials are evaluating whether awake proning benefits non-COVID hypoxemic respiratory failure.
Extending prone sessions beyond 16 hours to 24-48 hours has not consistently demonstrated additional mortality benefit.

strengths_limitations:
- **Strengths**: Comprehensive synthesis of physiological, clinical trial, and guideline evidence across intubated and non-intubated ARDS populations.
- **Limitations**: Much of the awake prone positioning evidence is derived from COVID-19 cohorts; optimal duration individualization tools (EIT, esophageal pressure) lack randomized outcome validation.
